summary:
H.R. 8752, the "Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2025," is a regular annual appropriations bill providing discretionary funding for DHS for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2025. As engrossed in the House, the bill's text reflects numerous parenthetical floor amendments (increases/reductions to account totals). It is organized in five titles and appropriates funds by account (Operations and Support; Procurement, Construction, and Improvements (PC&I); Research and Development; Federal Assistance), with account-specific availability periods and provisos.

**Title I (Departmental Management)** funds the Office of the Secretary, Management Directorate, Office of Intelligence and Analysis, and OIG. Administrative provisions impose reporting requirements (e.g., Sec. 101–102 IG and CFO reports), condition Treasury Forfeiture Fund transfers under 31 U.S.C. 9705(g)(4)(B) on prior notification (Sec. 103), and require quarterly acquisition-program briefings on Level 1/Level 2 programs (Sec. 105). Sec. 106 prohibits obligation for new pilots/demonstrations (defined as >10 FTE or ≥$5,000,000) absent documented objectives and reporting.

**Title II (Security, Enforcement, Investigations)** funds CBP, ICE, TSA, Coast Guard, and Secret Service. Notable directives: ICE funding must maintain not less than 50,000 detention beds and prioritize full-capacity detention with mandatory GPS Alternatives to Detention (Sec. 228); Sec. 211 allocates CBP PC&I funds, mandating steel bollard barriers 18–30 feet high per the August 1, 2020 Border Security Improvement Plan, with obligation beginning within 120 days. Numerous limitation riders defund specified policies: CBP One parole use (Sec. 213), the "Emergency Driving" directive (Sec. 214), the September 30, 2021 enforcement-priorities memorandum (Sec. 224), gender-affirming care (Sec. 227), and border-crossing fees (Sec. 207). Secs. 250–251 (effective 30 and 180 days after enactment, respectively) prohibit TRICARE cost-sharing for contraceptives and authorize 365-day contraceptive supply for Coast Guard beneficiaries under 10 U.S.C. 1074g/1075/1075a.

**Title III (Preparedness/Response)** funds CISA, FEMA, the Disaster Relief Fund ($22,741,000,000, designated under BBEDCA §251(b)(2)(D)), the National Flood Insurance Fund, and enumerated FEMA grant programs under the Homeland Security Act (6 U.S.C. 604–609a) and other statutes.

**Title IV** funds USCIS (E-Verify), FLETC, S&T, and CWMD. Sec. 406 authorizes an H-2B numerical-cap increase above INA §214(g)(1)(B).

**Title V (General Provisions)** sets reprogramming/transfer thresholds (Sec. 503; 5% transfer, 10% augmentation ceilings, June 15 cutoff). It rescinds $600,000,000 in prior-year CBP barrier funds (Public Law 116-260) (Sec. 550) and $154,000,000 from the Nonrecurring Expenses Fund (Sec. 551). Additional riders defund the "Circumvention of Lawful Pathways" and "Public Charge" rules, the Disinformation Governance Board, DHS equity/environmental-justice initiatives and enumerated Executive Orders, reduce a named employee's salary to $1 (Sec. 563), and prohibit funding Secretary Mayorkas's salary (Sec. 564).

This measure constitutes budget authority, not permanent authorizing law; provisions apply for fiscal year 2025 unless otherwise specified.
